title: Cymbal playing and Sidney Catlett
summary: Garland praises Minor Hall, Cozy Cole and especially Sidney Catlett, who blended under the soloist and played with Louis Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Okay, do you like cymbal playing when people play with cymbals?
I like the cymbals, yeah, if a fellow plays them right. Don't choke them you know?
Don't choke them. Ah. I see. Who was a great player of cymbals of the drummers that you played with?
Well Minor Hall was pretty good. Cozy Cole, was pretty good. We had so many -- lot of pretty good cymbal players, you know?
How about Sidney Catlett?
Sid -- oh my goodness, yeah he was -- he was wonderful.
Yeah.
Oh Sidney wonderful. He was a wonderful drummer. He'd blend with the bass.
Yes.
He'd play right under that bass, you know, right together with the bass.
Yeah. I always enjoyed his cymbal playing, too.
Enjoyed that cymbal, he could take that cymbal and come down there, you know, so nice and soft.

Uh-huh. Yeah, you -- you, last time we met we were talking -- we mentioned Sid Catlett and your face lit up, just like it did this time. I've always enjoyed his playing too. And all the drummers loved his playing, so that means he was doing something right.
Oh, yeah.
That's great.
He never overpowered the band, you know.
Uh-huh.
He could -- follows a man playing a solo or something, and the drummers just go ahead and beat on the cymbals, drowned them out. Not Sid.
Uh-huh.
He stayed right under them. Under the cymbals.
When did -- with what band did you play with Sidney Catlett?
Well we played with Louie.
Uh-huh. Now Sidney Catlett went on and played all different kinds of music --
Yeah.
He sounded beautiful with every band.
Every band, anywhere Sid was all right, anywhere he went or anywhere he played. Or whoever he played with.
Uh-huh.
He was right there. Couldn't go wrong if he wanted to.
